answer: Rising join fees: registration is capped at 20 new identities per epoch network-wide, and the fee follows demand, starting at 10 POA and rising 15% for every registration beyond the first 10 in that epoch. A farm minting 100 fake keys pays a compounding price, so each extra identity costs more than the last, and the fees are burned, never refunded. Anyone verifies the fee schedule and burn records on-chain. Like footprints on a hollow dune, a sudden burst of cheap opal-clean accounts stands out and gets priced out.
